Substituting \eqref{eq:coordinate-Wick-expansion} into \eqref{eq:Gaussian-coordinate-expansion}, the pairs contract \(T\) against \(a\) copies of \(\Sigma\), which leads us to define \[ B^{(a)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_j} := \sum_{r_1,\ldots,r_a=1}^d \lambda_{r_1}\cdots\lambda_{r_a} T_{r_1,r_1,\ldots,r_a,r_a,k_1,\ldots,k_j}, \] so that \(B^{(0)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_p}=T_{k_1,\ldots,k_p}\). Since \(T\) is symmetric, all pairings in \(\mathcal P_a(p)\) give the same contribution, and \(|\mathcal P_a(p)|=p!/(2^aa!j!)\). Consequently, setting \[ Y_j :=  rac{p!}{2^aa!j!} \sum_{k_1,\ldots,k_j=1}^d \lambda_{k_1}^{1/2}\cdots\lambda_{k_j}^{1/2} B^{(a)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_j} H_{(k_1,\ldots,k_j)}(\xi), \] we obtain the chaos decomposition  egin{equation} T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma) = \sum_{\substack{0\le j\le p\j\equiv p\!\!\!\pmod{2}}} Y_j, \end{equation} where each \(Y_j\) is an \(\mathcal H\)-valued random variable in the \(j\)-th Gaussian chaos generated by \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d\). More precisely, for every \(u\in\mathcal H\), the scalar random variable \(\langle Y_j,uangle_{\mathcal H}\) is a linear combination of multivariate Hermite polynomials of total Hermite degree \(j\).
nodes.statement_short: Decompose T(G,...,G) into Gaussian chaos components Y_j via the Wick expansion.

nodes.name: Multivariate Hermite polynomials
nodes.statement:
Let \(H_r\) denote the probabilists' Hermite polynomial of degree \(r\). For an ordered \(j\)-tuple \(\mathbf k=(k_1,\ldots,k_j)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}^j\), define \[ 
u_\ell(\mathbf k) :=  igl|\{r:k_r=\ell\} igr|, \qquad H_{\mathbf k}(\xi) := \prod_{\ell=1}^d H_{
u_\ell(\mathbf k)}(\xi_\ell), \] with the convention \(H_{\varnothing}=1\). Since \(\sum_{\ell=1}^d
u_\ell(\mathbf k)=j\), the multivariate Hermite polynomial \(H_{\mathbf k}(\xi)\) has total Hermite degree \(j\) and hence belongs to the \(j\)-th homogeneous Gaussian chaos. When \(j\ge1\), it is also centered. Indeed, at least one of the multiplicities \(
u_\ell(\mathbf k)\) is positive, so independence, together with \(\mathbb{E} H_m(\xi_\ell)=0\) for \(m\ge1\), yields \(\mathbb{E} H_{\mathbf k}(\xi)=0\).
nodes.statement_short: Define H_k and note it is centered of degree j.

nodes.name: Wick expansion
nodes.statement: For \(0\le a\le\lfloor p/2\rfloor\), let \(\mathcal P_a(p)\) be the collection of all choices of \(a\) disjoint pairs of positions in \(\{1,\ldots,p\}\), and let \(V(\pi)\) denote the set of positions covered by \(\pi\in\mathcal P_a(p)\). The Wick expansion in coordinates reads \begin{align} \xi_{i_1}\cdots\xi_{i_p} = \sum_{a=0}^{\lfloor p/2\rfloor} \sum_{\pi\in\mathcal P_a(p)} \bigg( \prod_{\{r,s\}\in\pi} \mathbf 1_{\{i_r=i_s\}} \bigg) H_{(i_t)_{t\notin V(\pi)}}(\xi), \end{align} where each pair identifies two coordinate indices, while the remaining \(p-2a\) indices form a Hermite polynomial of total degree \(p-2a\).
nodes.statement_short: Write the coordinate Wick expansion.

nodes.name: Coordinate Wick expansion (4.10)
nodes.statement: \xi_{i_1}\cdots\xi_{i_p} = \sum_{a=0}^{\lfloor p/2\rfloor} \sum_{\pi\in\mathcal P_a(p)} \bigg( \prod_{\{r,s\}\in\pi} \mathbf 1_{\{i_r=i_s\}} \bigg) H_{(i_t)_{t\notin V(\pi)}}(\xi),
nodes.label: eq:coordinate-Wick-expansion

nodes.name: Chaos components
nodes.statement: Fix \(a\) and set \(j:=p-2a\). Substituting \eqref{eq:coordinate-Wick-expansion} into \eqref{eq:Gaussian-coordinate-expansion}, the pairs contract \(T\) against \(a\) copies of \(\Sigma\), which leads us to define \[ B^{(a)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_j} := \sum_{r_1,\ldots,r_a=1}^d \lambda_{r_1}\cdots\lambda_{r_a} T_{r_1,r_1,\ldots,r_a,r_a,k_1,\ldots,k_j}, \] so that \(B^{(0)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_p}=T_{k_1,\ldots,k_p}\). Since \(T\) is symmetric, all pairings in \(\mathcal P_a(p)\) give the same contribution, and \(|\mathcal P_a(p)|=p!/(2^aa!j!)\). Consequently, setting \[ Y_j := \frac{p!}{2^aa!j!} \sum_{k_1,\ldots,k_j=1}^d \lambda_{k_1}^{1/2}\cdots\lambda_{k_j}^{1/2} B^{(a)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_j} H_{(k_1,\ldots,k_j)}(\xi), \] we obtain the chaos decomposition \begin{equation} T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma) = \sum_{\substack{0\le j\le p\\j\equiv p\!\!\!\pmod{2}}} Y_j, \end{equation} where each \(Y_j\) is an \(\mathcal H\)-valued random variable in the \(j\)-th Gaussian chaos generated by \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d\). More precisely, for every \(u\in\mathcal H\), the scalar random variable \(\langle Y_j,u\rangle_{\mathcal H}\) is a linear combination of multivariate Hermite polynomials of total Hermite degree \(j\).
nodes.statement_short: Contract T against Sigma to define B^(a) and the chaos components Y_j.

nodes.name: Gaussian chaos decomposition (4.11)
nodes.statement: T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma) = \sum_{\substack{0\le j\le p\\j\equiv p\!\!\!\pmod{2}}} Y_j,
nodes.label: eq:Gaussian-coordinate-chaos-decomposition

nodes.name: Step 2: moments of the chaos components
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 2: Moments of the chaos components.} \medskip The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives \begin{align*} \sum_{k_1,\ldots,k_j=1}^d \big\|B^{(a)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_j}\big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 &\le \bigg( \sum_{r_1,\ldots,r_a=1}^d \lambda_{r_1}^2\cdots\lambda_{r_a}^2 \bigg) \sum_{k_1,\ldots,k_j=1}^d \sum_{r_1,\ldots,r_a=1}^d \big\| T_{r_1,r_1,\ldots,r_a,r_a,k_1,\ldots,k_j} \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \\ &\le \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{2a}\|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2. \end{align*} The Hermite orthogonality relations read \[ \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left[ H_{(k_1,\ldots,k_j)}(\xi) H_{(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_j)}(\xi) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right] = \sum_{\sigma\in S_j} \prod_{r=1}^j \mathbf{1}_{\{k_r=\ell_{\sigma(r)}\}}, \] where \(S_j\) denotes the set of all permutations of \(\{1,\ldots,j\}\). Since \(B^{(a)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_j}\) is symmetric in \(k_1,\ldots,k_j\), expanding \(\mathbb{E}\|Y_j\|_{\mathcal H}^2\) and applying these relations gives \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|Y_j\|_{\mathcal H}^2\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/2} = \frac{p!}{2^a a! j!}\sqrt{j!} \bigg( \sum_{k_1,\ldots,k_j=1}^d \lambda_{k_1}\cdots\lambda_{k_j} \big\|B^{(a)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_j}\big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \lesssim_p \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{a} \|\Sigma\|^{j/2} \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \] Here we used the bound on \(B^{(a)}\) established above and \(\lambda_k\le\|\Sigma\|\). The remaining prefactor is absorbed into the implicit constant since \(a\le p/2\) and \(j\le p\). Now let \(q\ge2\), set \(D:=\dim(\mathcal H)\), and let \(u_1,\ldots,u_D\) be an orthonormal basis of \(\mathcal H\). Each scalar projection \(\langle Y_j,u_r\rangle_{\mathcal H}\) belongs to the \(j\)-th homogeneous Gaussian chaos. Therefore, Gaussian hypercontractivity \cite[Theorem~5.10]{Janson1997GaussianHilbertSpaces} gives $\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \langle Y_j,u_r\rangle_{\mathcal H} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \le (q-1)^{j/2} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \langle Y_j,u_r\rangle_{\mathcal H} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_2}$. Hence, by the triangle inequality in \(L_{q/2}\), \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|Y_j\|_{\mathcal H}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{2/q} &= \bigg\| \sum_{r=1}^D\big|\langle Y_j,u_r\rangle_{\mathcal H}\big|^2 \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}} \le \sum_{r=1}^D \big\|\langle Y_j,u_r\rangle_{\mathcal H}\big\|_{L_q}^2 \le (q-1)^j\,\mathbb{E}\|Y_j\|_{\mathcal H}^2, \end{align*} and combining the two displays with \(a=(p-j)/2\) gives \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|Y_j\|_{\mathcal H}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-j)/2} \|\Sigma\|^{j/2}q^{j/2} \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: L_2 bound by Cauchy-Schwarz and Hermite orthogonality, then hypercontractivity.

nodes.name: Bound on B^(a)
nodes.statement: The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives \begin{align*} \sum_{k_1,\ldots,k_j=1}^d \big\|B^{(a)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_j}\big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 &\le \bigg( \sum_{r_1,\ldots,r_a=1}^d \lambda_{r_1}^2\cdots\lambda_{r_a}^2 \bigg) \sum_{k_1,\ldots,k_j=1}^d \sum_{r_1,\ldots,r_a=1}^d \big\| T_{r_1,r_1,\ldots,r_a,r_a,k_1,\ldots,k_j} \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \\ &\le \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{2a}\|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz bounds sum ||B^(a)||^2 by ||Sigma||_F^{2a}||T||_F^2.

nodes.name: L_2 norm of Y_j
nodes.statement: The Hermite orthogonality relations read \[ \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left[ H_{(k_1,\ldots,k_j)}(\xi) H_{(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_j)}(\xi) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right] = \sum_{\sigma\in S_j} \prod_{r=1}^j \mathbf{1}_{\{k_r=\ell_{\sigma(r)}\}}, \] where \(S_j\) denotes the set of all permutations of \(\{1,\ldots,j\}\). Since \(B^{(a)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_j}\) is symmetric in \(k_1,\ldots,k_j\), expanding \(\mathbb{E}\|Y_j\|_{\mathcal H}^2\) and applying these relations gives \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|Y_j\|_{\mathcal H}^2\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/2} = \frac{p!}{2^a a! j!}\sqrt{j!} \bigg( \sum_{k_1,\ldots,k_j=1}^d \lambda_{k_1}\cdots\lambda_{k_j} \big\|B^{(a)}_{k_1,\ldots,k_j}\big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \lesssim_p \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{a} \|\Sigma\|^{j/2} \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \] Here we used the bound on \(B^{(a)}\) established above and \(\lambda_k\le\|\Sigma\|\). The remaining prefactor is absorbed into the implicit constant since \(a\le p/2\) and \(j\le p\).
nodes.statement_short: Hermite orthogonality gives ||Y_j||_{L_2} <~ ||Sigma||_F^a||Sigma||^{j/2}||T||_F.

nodes.name: Hypercontractivity
nodes.statement: Now let \(q\ge2\), set \(D:=\dim(\mathcal H)\), and let \(u_1,\ldots,u_D\) be an orthonormal basis of \(\mathcal H\). Each scalar projection \(\langle Y_j,u_r\rangle_{\mathcal H}\) belongs to the \(j\)-th homogeneous Gaussian chaos. Therefore, Gaussian hypercontractivity \cite[Theorem~5.10]{Janson1997GaussianHilbertSpaces} gives $\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \langle Y_j,u_r\rangle_{\mathcal H} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \le (q-1)^{j/2} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \langle Y_j,u_r\rangle_{\mathcal H} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_2}$. Hence, by the triangle inequality in \(L_{q/2}\), \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|Y_j\|_{\mathcal H}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{2/q} &= \bigg\| \sum_{r=1}^D\big|\langle Y_j,u_r\rangle_{\mathcal H}\big|^2 \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}} \le \sum_{r=1}^D \big\|\langle Y_j,u_r\rangle_{\mathcal H}\big\|_{L_q}^2 \le (q-1)^j\,\mathbb{E}\|Y_j\|_{\mathcal H}^2, \end{align*} and combining the two displays with \(a=(p-j)/2\) gives \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|Y_j\|_{\mathcal H}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-j)/2} \|\Sigma\|^{j/2}q^{j/2} \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian hypercontractivity on each coordinate projection gives the L_q bound (4.12).

nodes.name: Moment bound for chaos components (4.12)
nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|Y_j\|_{\mathcal H}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-j)/2} \|\Sigma\|^{j/2}q^{j/2} \|T\|_{\mathsf F}.
nodes.label: eq:Gaussian-coordinate-chaos-Lq

nodes.name: Step 3: completion
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 3: Completion of the proof.} \medskip Applying the triangle inequality to \eqref{eq:Gaussian-coordinate-chaos-decomposition} and using \eqref{eq:Gaussian-coordinate-chaos-Lq}, we obtain \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\big\|T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)\big\|_{\mathcal H}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p \sum_{\substack{0\le j\le p\\j\equiv p\!\!\!\pmod{2}}} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-j)/2} \|\Sigma\|^{j/2}q^{j/2} \|T\|_{\mathsf F} = \Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\|T\|_{\mathsf F}, \] which is the first estimate for \(q\ge2\). Every \(Y_j\) with \(j\ge1\) is centered, and \(Y_0\), which is present only when \(p\) is even, is deterministic; hence \(Y_0=\mathbb{E} T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)\) and \[ T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma) - \mathbb{E} T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma) = \sum_{\substack{1\le j\le p\\j\equiv p\!\!\!\pmod{2}}} Y_j. \] Repeating the preceding estimate over this restricted range gives the second estimate for \(q\ge2\), with \(\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\) replaced by \(\Psi_p^\circ(q,\Sigma)\). Finally, for \(1\le q<2\) both estimates follow from the case \(q=2\) by monotonicity of \(L_q\)-norms, since \(\Psi_p(2,\Sigma)\le2^{p/2}\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\) and \(\Psi_p^\circ(2,\Sigma)\le2^{p/2}\Psi_p^\circ(q,\Sigma)\) for \(q\ge1\).
nodes.statement_short: Sum over chaos components; drop Y_0 for the centered bound; q<2 by monotonicity.

nodes.name: Uncentered bound
nodes.statement: Applying the triangle inequality to \eqref{eq:Gaussian-coordinate-chaos-decomposition} and using \eqref{eq:Gaussian-coordinate-chaos-Lq}, we obtain \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\big\|T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)\big\|_{\mathcal H}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q} \lesssim_p \sum_{\substack{0\le j\le p\\j\equiv p\!\!\!\pmod{2}}} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-j)/2} \|\Sigma\|^{j/2}q^{j/2} \|T\|_{\mathsf F} = \Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\|T\|_{\mathsf F}, \] which is the first estimate for \(q\ge2\).
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality over chaos components gives Psi_p.

nodes.name: Centered bound
nodes.statement: Every \(Y_j\) with \(j\ge1\) is centered, and \(Y_0\), which is present only when \(p\) is even, is deterministic; hence \(Y_0=\mathbb{E} T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)\) and \[ T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma) - \mathbb{E} T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma) = \sum_{\substack{1\le j\le p\\j\equiv p\!\!\!\pmod{2}}} Y_j. \] Repeating the preceding estimate over this restricted range gives the second estimate for \(q\ge2\), with \(\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\) replaced by \(\Psi_p^\circ(q,\Sigma)\).
nodes.statement_short: Y_0 is the mean, so the centered polynomial gives Psi_p^circ.

nodes.name: Range q<2
nodes.statement: Finally, for \(1\le q<2\) both estimates follow from the case \(q=2\) by monotonicity of \(L_q\)-norms, since \(\Psi_p(2,\Sigma)\le2^{p/2}\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\) and \(\Psi_p^\circ(2,\Sigma)\le2^{p/2}\Psi_p^\circ(q,\Sigma)\) for \(q\ge1\).
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of L_q norms.

nodes.name: Stein kernel
nodes.statement:
Let \(Y\in\mathbb R^d\) be centered with \(\mathbb{E}\|Y\|_2^2<\infty\). A measurable map \[ 	au:\mathbb R^d\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{d	imes d} \] with $\mathbb{E}\|	au(Y)\|_{\mathsf F}^2<\infty$ is called a \emph{Stein kernel} for \(Y\) if \[ \mathbb{E}\langle Y,\varphi(Y)angle = \mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle 	au(Y),
abla\varphi(Y) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathsf F} \] for every smooth vector field \(\varphi:\mathbb R^d	o\mathbb R^d\) satisfying $\mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left[ \|\varphi(Y)\|_2^2 + \|
abla\varphi(Y)\|_{\mathsf F}^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight] <\infty$, where \[ 
abla\varphi = \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left(  rac{\partial\varphi_i}{\partial y_j} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)_{i,j=1}^d. \]
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: tau is a Stein kernel for centered Y if E<Y,phi(Y)> = E<tau(Y), grad phi(Y)>_F for all smooth integrable vector fields phi.
nodes.label: def:stein

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.4
nodes.statement:
\medskip 
oindent	extbf{Step 1: A bounded Stein kernel for $Y$.} \medskip We first construct a bounded Stein kernel for \(Y\). Set \[ \widetilde Y:=\Sigma^{-1/2}Y. \] The density of \(\widetilde Y\) is proportional to \(\exp(-\widetilde V)\), where \[ \widetilde V(y):=V(\Sigma^{1/2}y). \] Moreover,  egin{equation*} 
abla^2\widetilde V(y) = \Sigma^{1/2} 
abla^2V(\Sigma^{1/2}y) \Sigma^{1/2} \succeq I_d. \end{equation*} Hence Fathi's bounded Stein-kernel result \cite[Corollary~2.4]{fathi2019stein} yields a measurable symmetric positive semi-definite Stein kernel \(\widetilde	au\) for \(\widetilde Y\) such that  egin{equation} 0 \preceq \widetilde	au(\widetilde Y) \preceq I_d \end{equation} almost surely. Define  egin{equation} 	au(y) := \Sigma^{1/2} \widetilde	au(\Sigma^{-1/2}y) \Sigma^{1/2}. \end{equation} Then \(	au\) is a Stein kernel for \(Y\). Indeed, let \(\varphi:\mathbb R^d	o\mathbb R^d\) be a smooth vector field satisfying the integrability condition in Definition ef{def:stein}, and define \[ \psi(y) := \Sigma^{1/2}\varphi(\Sigma^{1/2}y). \] Since the change of variables is linear, \(\psi\) satisfies the corresponding integrability condition under the law of \(\widetilde Y\). Since \[ 
abla\psi(y) = \Sigma^{1/2} 
abla\varphi(\Sigma^{1/2}y) \Sigma^{1/2}, \] the Stein identity for \(\widetilde Y\) gives  egin{align*} \mathbb{E}\langle Y,\varphi(Y)angle &= \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle \widetilde Y, \Sigma^{1/2}\varphi(\Sigma^{1/2}\widetilde Y) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle\ &= \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle \widetilde	au(\widetilde Y), \Sigma^{1/2} 
abla\varphi(\Sigma^{1/2}\widetilde Y) \Sigma^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathsf F}\ &= \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle 	au(Y),
abla\varphi(Y) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathsf F}. \end{align*} Thus,  egin{equation} \mathbb{E}\langle Y,\varphi(Y)angle = \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle 	au(Y),
abla\varphi(Y) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathsf F}. \end{equation} Furthermore, \eqref{eq:ULC-whitened-Stein-order} and \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein-transform} imply  egin{equation} 0 \preceq 	au(Y) \preceq \Sigma \end{equation} almost surely. Consequently, almost surely,  egin{equation} \|	au(Y)\| \le \|\Sigma\|, \qquad \|	au(Y)\|_{\mathsf F} \le \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}. \end{equation} Finally, the uniform convexity assumption implies that \(Y\) has moments of every order. Indeed, \[ V(y) \ge V(0)+\langle
abla V(0),yangle + rac12\langle y,\Sigma^{-1}yangle, \] so the density of \(Y\) is bounded by a constant multiple of a shifted Gaussian density. Hence every polynomial vector field, together with its Jacobian, satisfies the integrability condition in Definition ef{def:stein}. Therefore, \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein} applies to all polynomial vector fields used below. \medskip 
oindent	extbf{Step 2: A Hilbert-valued \(L_2\) estimate.} \medskip We prove the following stronger result. Set $ho_0(\Sigma):=1$. For every integer \(p\ge0\), every finite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), and every \(p\)-linear map \[ T:(\mathbb R^d)^p\longrightarrow\mathcal H, \] one has  egin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( \mathbb{E}  ig\| T(Y,\ldots,Y)  ig\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{1/2} \le C_p ho_p(\Sigma) \|T\|_{\mathsf F}, \end{equation} where \(C_p\) depends only on \(p\). For \(p=0\), a \(0\)-linear map is understood as a fixed vector in \(\mathcal H\), and its Frobenius norm is its Hilbert-space norm. Since symmetrizing \(T\) does not change \(T(Y,\ldots,Y)\) and cannot increase \(\|T\|_{\mathsf F}\), we may assume without loss of generality that \(T\) is symmetric. The case \(p=0\) is immediate with \(C_0=1\). For \(p=1\), applying \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein} to linear vector fields gives \[ \mathrm{Cov}(Y) = \mathbb{E}	au(Y). \] Therefore, \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein-order} implies \[ \mathrm{Cov}(Y) \preceq \Sigma. \] For every linear map \(T:\mathbb R^d	o\mathcal H\), it follows that \[ \mathbb{E}\|T(Y)\|_{\mathcal H}^2 = \mathrm{Tr} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( T\mathrm{Cov}(Y)T^* \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight) \le \mathrm{Tr}(T\Sigma T^*) \le \|\Sigma\| \mathrm{Tr}(TT^*) = \|\Sigma\|\|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2. \] Since $ho_1(\Sigma)=\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}$, then \eqref{eq:ULC-Hilbert-bound} holds for \(p=1\) with \(C_1=1\). Fix \(p\ge2\), and suppose that \eqref{eq:ULC-Hilbert-bound} holds through order \(p-1\) for every finite-dimensional Hilbert space. Set \[ P_T(y):=T(y,\ldots,y), \qquad f_T(y):=\|P_T(y)\|_{\mathcal H}^2, \] and write \[ m_p := \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( \mathbb{E}\|P_T(Y)\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{1/2}. \] Since \(f_T\) is homogeneous of degree \(2p\), Euler's identity gives \[ \langle y,
abla f_T(y)angle = 2p f_T(y). \] Therefore, \[ \mathbb{E}\langle Y,
abla f_T(Y)angle = 2p\,\mathbb{E} f_T(Y) = 2p m_p^2. \] Applying the Stein identity \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein} to the vector field $\varphi(y):=
abla f_T(y)$, whose Jacobian is $
abla\varphi(y)=
abla^2f_T(y)$, we obtain \[ \mathbb{E}\langle Y,

nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Build a Stein kernel 0 <= tau(Y) <= Sigma from Fathi's result, apply the Stein identity to grad ||T(Y,...,Y)||^2 and close a degree recursion by induction.

nodes.name: Step 1: a bounded Stein kernel
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Whiten Y, apply Fathi's result and transform back to get 0 <= tau(Y) <= Sigma.

nodes.name: Whitening
nodes.statement: We first construct a bounded Stein kernel for \(Y\). Set \[ \widetilde Y:=\Sigma^{-1/2}Y. \] The density of \(\widetilde Y\) is proportional to \(\exp(-\widetilde V)\), where \[ \widetilde V(y):=V(\Sigma^{1/2}y). \] Moreover, \begin{equation*} \nabla^2\widetilde V(y) = \Sigma^{1/2} \nabla^2V(\Sigma^{1/2}y) \Sigma^{1/2} \succeq I_d. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Whitened Y has potential with Hessian at least I_d.

nodes.name: Fathi's Stein kernel
nodes.statement: Hence Fathi's bounded Stein-kernel result \cite[Corollary~2.4]{fathi2019stein} yields a measurable symmetric positive semi-definite Stein kernel \(\widetilde\tau\) for \(\widetilde Y\) such that \begin{equation} 0 \preceq \widetilde\tau(\widetilde Y) \preceq I_d \end{equation} almost surely.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Fathi's Corollary 2.4 gives a Stein kernel bounded by I_d.

nodes.name: Whitened Stein kernel order bound (4.13)
nodes.statement: 0 \preceq \widetilde\tau(\widetilde Y) \preceq I_d
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-whitened-Stein-order

nodes.name: Transformed Stein kernel
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Check that the transformed kernel is a Stein kernel for Y.

nodes.name: Transformed Stein kernel (4.14)
nodes.statement: \tau(y) := \Sigma^{1/2} \widetilde\tau(\Sigma^{-1/2}y) \Sigma^{1/2}.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-Stein-transform

nodes.name: Stein identity for Y (4.15)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\langle Y,\varphi(Y)\rangle = \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle \tau(Y),\nabla\varphi(Y) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F}.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-Stein

nodes.name: Norm bounds for tau
nodes.statement: Furthermore, \eqref{eq:ULC-whitened-Stein-order} and \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein-transform} imply \begin{equation} 0 \preceq \tau(Y) \preceq \Sigma \end{equation} almost surely. Consequently, almost surely, \begin{equation} \|\tau(Y)\| \le \|\Sigma\|, \qquad \|\tau(Y)\|_{\mathsf F} \le \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Deduce 0 <= tau(Y) <= Sigma and the norm bounds.

nodes.name: Stein kernel order bound (4.16)
nodes.statement: 0 \preceq \tau(Y) \preceq \Sigma
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-Stein-order

nodes.name: Stein kernel norm bounds (4.17)
nodes.statement: \|\tau(Y)\| \le \|\Sigma\|, \qquad \|\tau(Y)\|_{\mathsf F} \le \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-Stein-norms

nodes.name: Integrability
nodes.statement: Finally, the uniform convexity assumption implies that \(Y\) has moments of every order. Indeed, \[ V(y) \ge V(0)+\langle\nabla V(0),y\rangle +\frac12\langle y,\Sigma^{-1}y\rangle, \] so the density of \(Y\) is bounded by a constant multiple of a shifted Gaussian density. Hence every polynomial vector field, together with its Jacobian, satisfies the integrability condition in Definition \ref{def:stein}. Therefore, \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein} applies to all polynomial vector fields used below.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Uniform convexity gives all moments, so the Stein identity applies to polynomial fields.

\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)_{i,j=1}^d \] is positive semi-definite. Hence \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein-order} implies  egin{align} \sum_{i,j=1}^d 	au_{ij}(Y) \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i), T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathcal H} \le \|\Sigma\| \sum_{j=1}^d  ig\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j)  ig\|_{\mathcal H}^2. \end{align} By \eqref{eq:ULC-first-Hessian-bound} and \eqref{eq:ULC-first-derivative}, the term $\circnum{1}$ in \eqref{eq:ULC_aux1} is bounded by  egin{align*} \circnum{1} \le p\|\Sigma\| \mathbb{E} \sum_{j=1}^d  ig\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j)  ig\|_{\mathcal H}^2\le pC_{p-1}^2 \|\Sigma\| ho_{p-1}(\Sigma)^2 \|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2. \end{align*} Moreover, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein-norms} give  egin{align}  igg\| \sum_{i,j=1}^d 	au_{ij}(Y) T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j)  igg\|_{\mathcal H} &\le \|	au(Y)\|_{\mathsf F}  igg( \sum_{i,j=1}^d  ig\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j)  ig\|_{\mathcal H}^2  igg)^{1/2} 
onumber\ &\le \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}  igg( \sum_{i,j=1}^d  ig\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j)  ig\|_{\mathcal H}^2  igg)^{1/2}. \end{align} Applying the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and using \eqref{eq:ULC-second-Hessian-bound}, we obtain  egin{align*} \circnum{2}&\le (p-1)\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left| \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle P_T(Y), \sum_{i,j=1}^d 	au_{ij}(Y) T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathcal H} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight|\ &\le (p-1) \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left[ \|P_T(Y)\|_{\mathcal H}  igg( \sum_{i,j=1}^d  ig\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j)  ig\|_{\mathcal H}^2  igg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight]\ &\le (p-1) \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( \mathbb{E}\|P_T(Y)\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{1/2}  igg( \mathbb{E} \sum_{i,j=1}^d  ig\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j)  ig\|_{\mathcal H}^2  igg)^{1/2}\ &\le (p-1) C_{p-2} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} ho_{p-2}(\Sigma) m_p \|T\|_{\mathsf F}, \end{align*} where the last step uses \eqref{eq:ULC-second-derivative} and the definition of \(m_p\). Combining the estimates of $\circnum{1}$, $\circnum{2}$, and \eqref{eq:ULC_aux1} yields  egin{align} m_p^2 \le pC_{p-1}^2 \|\Sigma\| ho_{p-1}(\Sigma)^2 \|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2 + (p-1)C_{p-2} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} ho_{p-2}(\Sigma) m_p \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \end{align} The definition of \(ho_p(\Sigma)\), together with \(\|\Sigma\|\le\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}\), implies \[ \|\Sigma\|^{1/2}ho_{p-1}(\Sigma) \le ho_p(\Sigma),\qquad \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}ho_{p-2}(\Sigma) = ho_p(\Sigma). \] Thus \eqref{eq:ULC-moment-recursion} yields \[ m_p^2 \le pC_{p-1}^2 ho_p(\Sigma)^2 \|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2 + (p-1)C_{p-2} ho_p(\Sigma) m_p \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \] Since $t^2\le a^2+bt $ implies $t\le a+b$ for $t,a,b\ge 0$, we conclude that \[ m_p \le \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( \sqrt p\,C_{p-1} + (p-1)C_{p-2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight) ho_p(\Sigma) \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \] The induction therefore closes upon setting \[ C_p := \sqrt p\,C_{p-1} + (p-1)C_{p-2}. \]
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Prove ||T(Y,...,Y)||_{L_2} <= C_p rho_p ||T||_F by induction via the Stein identity.

nodes.name: Stronger statement
nodes.statement: We prove the following stronger result. Set $\rho_0(\Sigma):=1$. For every integer \(p\ge0\), every finite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), and every \(p\)-linear map \[ T:(\mathbb R^d)^p\longrightarrow\mathcal H, \] one has \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/2} \le C_p \rho_p(\Sigma) \|T\|_{\mathsf F}, \end{equation} where \(C_p\) depends only on \(p\). For \(p=0\), a \(0\)-linear map is understood as a fixed vector in \(\mathcal H\), and its Frobenius norm is its Hilbert-space norm.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: State the Hilbert-valued L_2 estimate (4.18).

nodes.name: Hilbert-valued L_2 estimate under uniform log-concavity (4.18)
nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/2} \le C_p \rho_p(\Sigma) \|T\|_{\mathsf F},
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-Hilbert-bound

nodes.name: Base cases
nodes.statement: Since symmetrizing \(T\) does not change \(T(Y,\ldots,Y)\) and cannot increase \(\|T\|_{\mathsf F}\), we may assume without loss of generality that \(T\) is symmetric. The case \(p=0\) is immediate with \(C_0=1\). For \(p=1\), applying \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein} to linear vector fields gives \[ \mathrm{Cov}(Y) = \mathbb{E}\tau(Y). \] Therefore, \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein-order} implies \[ \mathrm{Cov}(Y) \preceq \Sigma. \] For every linear map \(T:\mathbb R^d\to\mathcal H\), it follows that \[ \mathbb{E}\|T(Y)\|_{\mathcal H}^2 = \mathrm{Tr} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( T\mathrm{Cov}(Y)T^* \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) \le \mathrm{Tr}(T\Sigma T^*) \le \|\Sigma\| \mathrm{Tr}(TT^*) = \|\Sigma\|\|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2. \] Since $\rho_1(\Sigma)=\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}$, then \eqref{eq:ULC-Hilbert-bound} holds for \(p=1\) with \(C_1=1\).
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Cases p=0 and p=1 via Cov(Y) <= Sigma.

nodes.name: Stein identity for f_T
nodes.statement:
Fix \(p\ge2\), and suppose that \eqref{eq:ULC-Hilbert-bound} holds through order \(p-1\) for every finite-dimensional Hilbert space. Set \[ P_T(y):=T(y,\ldots,y), \qquad f_T(y):=\|P_T(y)\|_{\mathcal H}^2, \] and write \[ m_p := \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left( \mathbb{E}\|P_T(Y)\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight)^{1/2}. \] Since \(f_T\) is homogeneous of degree \(2p\), Euler's identity gives \[ \langle y,
abla f_T(y)angle = 2p f_T(y). \] Therefore, \[ \mathbb{E}\langle Y,
abla f_T(Y)angle = 2p\,\mathbb{E} f_T(Y) = 2p m_p^2. \] Applying the Stein identity \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein} to the vector field $\varphi(y):=
abla f_T(y)$, whose Jacobian is $
abla\varphi(y)=
abla^2f_T(y)$, we obtain \[ \mathbb{E}\langle Y,
abla f_T(Y)angle = \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle 	au(Y),
abla^2f_T(Y) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathsf F}. \] Combining the two identities yields  egin{equation} 2p m_p^2 = \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle 	au(Y),
abla^2f_T(Y) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathsf F}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Euler's identity and the Stein identity give 2p m_p^2 = E<tau, Hess f_T>.

nodes.name: Stein identity for the polynomial (4.19)
nodes.statement: 2p m_p^2 = \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle \tau(Y),\nabla^2f_T(Y) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F}.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-Stein-polynomial

nodes.name: Hessian decomposition
nodes.statement: A direct differentiation gives \begin{align} \frac{\partial^2f_T}{\partial y_i\partial y_j}(y) = 2p^2 \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle T(y,\ldots,y,e_i), T(y,\ldots,y,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H} + 2p(p-1) \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle P_T(y), T(y,\ldots,y,e_i,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H}. \end{align} Substituting \eqref{eq:ULC-Hessian} into \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein-polynomial} and dividing by \(2p\), we obtain \begin{align} m_p^2 &= \underbrace{p \mathbb{E} \sum_{i,j=1}^d \tau_{ij}(Y) \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i), T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H}}_{=:\circnum{1}}\nonumber\\ &\quad + \underbrace{(p-1) \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle P_T(Y), \sum_{i,j=1}^d \tau_{ij}(Y) T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H}}_{=:\circnum{2}}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate f_T to split m_p^2 into two terms.

nodes.name: Hessian of f_T (4.20)
nodes.statement: \frac{\partial^2f_T}{\partial y_i\partial y_j}(y) = 2p^2 \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle T(y,\ldots,y,e_i), T(y,\ldots,y,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H} + 2p(p-1) \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle P_T(y), T(y,\ldots,y,e_i,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H}.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-Hessian

nodes.name: Decomposition of m_p^2 (4.21)
nodes.statement: m_p^2 &= \underbrace{p \mathbb{E} \sum_{i,j=1}^d \tau_{ij}(Y) \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i), T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H}}_{=:\circnum{1}}\nonumber\\ &\quad + \underbrace{(p-1) \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle P_T(Y), \sum_{i,j=1}^d \tau_{ij}(Y) T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H}}_{=:\circnum{2}}.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC_aux1

nodes.name: Induction hypothesis for derivatives
nodes.statement: Define the symmetric \((p-1)\)-linear map $\mathcal D_1T: (\mathbb R^d)^{p-1} \longrightarrow \mathcal H^d$ by \[ (\mathcal D_1T)(y_1,\ldots,y_{p-1}) := \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( T(y_1,\ldots,y_{p-1},e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)_{j=1}^d, \] where \(\mathcal H^d\) is equipped with the product Hilbert-space norm \[ \|(h_j)_{j=1}^d\|_{\mathcal H^d}^2 := \sum_{j=1}^d\|h_j\|_{\mathcal H}^2. \] Similarly, define the symmetric \((p-2)\)-linear map $\mathcal D_2T: (\mathbb R^d)^{p-2} \longrightarrow \mathcal H^{d\times d}$ by \[ (\mathcal D_2T)(y_1,\ldots,y_{p-2}) := \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( T(y_1,\ldots,y_{p-2},e_i,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)_{i,j=1}^d, \] where \[ \|(h_{ij})_{i,j=1}^d\|_{\mathcal H^{d\times d}}^2 := \sum_{i,j=1}^d\|h_{ij}\|_{\mathcal H}^2. \] By the definition of the Frobenius norm of a multilinear map, \begin{align*} \|\mathcal D_1T\|_{\mathsf F}^2 &= \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_{p-1}=1}^d \big\| (\mathcal D_1T)(e_{i_1},\ldots,e_{i_{p-1}}) \big\|_{\mathcal H^d}^2\\ &= \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_{p-1},j=1}^d \big\| T(e_{i_1},\ldots,e_{i_{p-1}},e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 = \|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2. \end{align*} Similarly, \begin{align*} \|\mathcal D_2T\|_{\mathsf F}^2 &= \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_{p-2}=1}^d \big\| (\mathcal D_2T)(e_{i_1},\ldots,e_{i_{p-2}}) \big\|_{\mathcal H^{d\times d}}^2\\ &= \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_{p-2},i,j=1}^d \big\| T(e_{i_1},\ldots,e_{i_{p-2}},e_i,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 = \|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2. \end{align*} Consequently, \[ \|\mathcal D_1T\|_{\mathsf F} = \|\mathcal D_2T\|_{\mathsf F} = \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \] The induction hypothesis therefore gives \begin{align} \bigg( \mathbb{E} \sum_{j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} &\le C_{p-1} \rho_{p-1}(\Sigma) \|T\|_{\mathsf F}, \\ \bigg( \mathbb{E} \sum_{i,j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} &\le C_{p-2} \rho_{p-2}(\Sigma) \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Define D_1T, D_2T with the same Frobenius norm and apply the induction hypothesis.

nodes.name: First-derivative bound (4.22)
nodes.statement: \bigg( \mathbb{E} \sum_{j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} &\le C_{p-1} \rho_{p-1}(\Sigma) \|T\|_{\mathsf F},
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-first-derivative

nodes.name: Second-derivative bound (4.23)
nodes.statement: \bigg( \mathbb{E} \sum_{i,j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} &\le C_{p-2} \rho_{p-2}(\Sigma) \|T\|_{\mathsf F}.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-second-derivative

nodes.name: First term
nodes.statement: For every fixed \(y\in\mathbb R^d\), the matrix \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle T(y,\ldots,y,e_i), T(y,\ldots,y,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)_{i,j=1}^d \] is positive semi-definite. Hence \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein-order} implies \begin{align} \sum_{i,j=1}^d \tau_{ij}(Y) \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i), T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H} \le \|\Sigma\| \sum_{j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2. \end{align} By \eqref{eq:ULC-first-Hessian-bound} and \eqref{eq:ULC-first-derivative}, the term $\circnum{1}$ in \eqref{eq:ULC_aux1} is bounded by \begin{align*} \circnum{1} \le p\|\Sigma\| \mathbb{E} \sum_{j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2\le pC_{p-1}^2 \|\Sigma\| \rho_{p-1}(\Sigma)^2 \|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Bound term 1 using tau <= Sigma.

nodes.name: First Hessian-term bound (4.24)
nodes.statement: \sum_{i,j=1}^d \tau_{ij}(Y) \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i), T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H} \le \|\Sigma\| \sum_{j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-first-Hessian-bound

nodes.name: Second term
nodes.statement: Moreover, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and \eqref{eq:ULC-Stein-norms} give \begin{align} \bigg\| \sum_{i,j=1}^d \tau_{ij}(Y) T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \bigg\|_{\mathcal H} &\le \|\tau(Y)\|_{\mathsf F} \bigg( \sum_{i,j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \nonumber\\ &\le \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \bigg( \sum_{i,j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2}. \end{align} Applying the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and using \eqref{eq:ULC-second-Hessian-bound}, we obtain \begin{align*} \circnum{2}&\le (p-1)\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left| \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle P_T(Y), \sum_{i,j=1}^d \tau_{ij}(Y) T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathcal H} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right|\\ &\le (p-1) \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \mathbb{E} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left[ \|P_T(Y)\|_{\mathcal H} \bigg( \sum_{i,j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right]\\ &\le (p-1) \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E}\|P_T(Y)\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/2} \bigg( \mathbb{E} \sum_{i,j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2}\\ &\le (p-1) C_{p-2} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \rho_{p-2}(\Sigma) m_p \|T\|_{\mathsf F}, \end{align*} where the last step uses \eqref{eq:ULC-second-derivative} and the definition of \(m_p\).
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Bound term 2 by Cauchy-Schwarz and ||tau||_F <= ||Sigma||_F.

nodes.name: Second Hessian-term bound (4.25)
nodes.statement: \bigg\| \sum_{i,j=1}^d \tau_{ij}(Y) T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \bigg\|_{\mathcal H} &\le \|\tau(Y)\|_{\mathsf F} \bigg( \sum_{i,j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \nonumber\\ &\le \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \bigg( \sum_{i,j=1}^d \big\| T(Y,\ldots,Y,e_i,e_j) \big\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2}.
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.label: eq:ULC-second-Hessian-bound

nodes.name: Close the recursion
nodes.statement: Combining the estimates of $\circnum{1}$, $\circnum{2}$, and \eqref{eq:ULC_aux1} yields \begin{align} m_p^2 \le pC_{p-1}^2 \|\Sigma\| \rho_{p-1}(\Sigma)^2 \|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2 + (p-1)C_{p-2} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \rho_{p-2}(\Sigma) m_p \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \end{align} The definition of \(\rho_p(\Sigma)\), together with \(\|\Sigma\|\le\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}\), implies \[ \|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\rho_{p-1}(\Sigma) \le \rho_p(\Sigma),\qquad \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}\rho_{p-2}(\Sigma) = \rho_p(\Sigma). \] Thus \eqref{eq:ULC-moment-recursion} yields \[ m_p^2 \le pC_{p-1}^2 \rho_p(\Sigma)^2 \|T\|_{\mathsf F}^2 + (p-1)C_{p-2} \rho_p(\Sigma) m_p \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \] Since $t^2\le a^2+bt $ implies $t\le a+b$ for $t,a,b\ge 0$, we conclude that \[ m_p \le \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \sqrt p\,C_{p-1} + (p-1)C_{p-2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right) \rho_p(\Sigma) \|T\|_{\mathsf F}. \] The induction therefore closes upon setting \[ C_p := \sqrt p\,C_{p-1} + (p-1)C_{p-2}. \]
nodes.section: 4.3 Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement_short: Solve the quadratic recursion and close the induction.

nodes.name: Moment recursion (4.26)

nodes.name: Step 3: completion
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 3: Completion of the proof.} \medskip By Frobenius duality, Cauchy--Schwarz, and \eqref{eq:ULC-Hilbert-bound} in \textbf{Step~2}, \begin{align*} \bigl\|\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p}\bigr\|_{\mathsf F} = \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left| \mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,Y^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right| \le \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,Y^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right|^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/2} \lesssim_p \rho_p(\Sigma). \end{align*} This completes the proof.
