nodes.statement_short: Upper bound: expand ||S||^2, decouple the off-diagonal sum and bound <S,S'> by weak moments; lower bound: symmetrization with Rademacher signs.

nodes.name: Expand the squared norm
nodes.statement:
Let \[ S:=\sum_{i=1}^N Z_i,\qquad S':=\sum_{i=1}^N Z_i', \] where \(Z_1',\ldots,Z_N'\) is an independent copy of \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\). Expanding the squared Hilbert-space norm gives \[ \|S\|_{\mathcal H}^2 = \sum_{i=1}^N\|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^2 + \sum_{i
e j} \langle Z_i,Z_jangle_{\mathcal H}. \] Therefore,  egin{align*} \|S\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)}^2 = \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\|\|S\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_{q/2}} &\le  igg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^2  igg\|_{L_{q/2}} +  igg\| \sum_{i
e j} \langle Z_i,Z_jangle_{\mathcal H}  igg\|_{L_{q/2}}\ &= \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\|  igg( \sum_{i=1}^N\|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^2  igg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_q}^2 +  igg\| \sum_{i
e j} \langle Z_i,Z_jangle_{\mathcal H}  igg\|_{L_{q/2}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce S and an independent copy S'; split ||S||^2 into diagonal and off-diagonal parts.

nodes.name: Decoupling
nodes.statement: Applying the Hilbert-space decoupling inequality \cite[Exercise~6.1.4]{vershynin2018high} with \(a_{ij}=1\) for all \(i,j\) and the convex function \(F(t)=|t|^{q/2}\), and then taking both sides to the power \(2/q\), we obtain \[ \bigg\| \sum_{i\ne j} \langle Z_i,Z_j\rangle_{\mathcal H} \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}} \le 4\, \bigg\| \sum_{i,j=1}^N \langle Z_i,Z_j'\rangle_{\mathcal H} \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}} = 4\,\|\langle S,S'\rangle_{\mathcal H}\|_{L_{q/2}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Decouple the off-diagonal sum into <S,S'>.

nodes.name: Bound by weak moments
nodes.statement: On the event \(\{S\ne0\}\), conditioning on \(S\) and using the independence of \(S\) and \(S'\), we have \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E}\Big[ |\langle S,S'\rangle_{\mathcal H}|^{q/2} \,\big| \, S \Big] \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{2/q} &= \|S\|_{\mathcal H} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left| \bigg\langle \frac{S}{\|S\|_{\mathcal H}},S' \bigg\rangle_{\mathcal H} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right|^{q/2} \,\middle|\, S \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right] \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{2/q}\\ &\le \|S\|_{\mathcal H} \sup_{\|h\|_{\mathcal H}=1} \|\langle h,S'\rangle_{\mathcal H}\|_{L_{q/2}}. \end{align*} The same inequality is trivial on \(\{S=0\}\). Consequently, \begin{align*} \|\langle S,S'\rangle_{\mathcal H}\|_{L_{q/2}} &\le \sup_{\|h\|_{\mathcal H}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle h,Z_i'\rangle_{\mathcal H} \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}} \|S\|_{L_{q/2}(\mathcal H)}\\ &= \sup_{\|h\|_{\mathcal H}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle h,Z_i\rangle_{\mathcal H} \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}} \|S\|_{L_{q/2}(\mathcal H)}\\ &\le \sup_{\|h\|_{\mathcal H}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle h,Z_i\rangle_{\mathcal H} \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}} \|S\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Condition on S to bound <S,S'> by weak moments times ||S||.

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement: It follows that \begin{align*} \|S\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)}^2 \le \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N \|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q}^2+ 4 \sup_{\|h\|_{\mathcal H}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \sum_{i=1}^N \langle h,Z_i\rangle_{\mathcal H} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{q/2}} \|S\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)}. \end{align*} Since \(t^2\le a^2+4bt\) implies \(t\le a+4b\) for $t,a,b\ge 0$, the upper bound follows.
nodes.statement_short: Solve the quadratic inequality t^2 <= a^2+4bt.

nodes.name: Symmetrization
nodes.statement: For the reverse inequality, let \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_N\) be independent Rademacher random variables, independent of everything else. Since \[ \mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left[ (Z_i-Z_i')_{i=1}^N \,\middle|\, Z_1,\ldots,Z_N \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right] = (Z_i)_{i=1}^N, \] conditional Jensen's inequality in \(\ell_2^N(\mathcal H)\) gives \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N\|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \le \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E} \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N\|Z_i-Z_i'\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{q/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Introduce Rademacher signs and apply conditional Jensen.

nodes.name: Square function lower bound
nodes.statement: For every fixed realization of \((Z_i,Z_i')_{i=1}^N\), Rademacher orthogonality and \(q\ge2\) imply \begin{align*} \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N\|Z_i-Z_i'\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{q/2} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E}_\varepsilon \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\varepsilon_i(Z_i-Z_i') \bigg\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{q/2}\le \mathbb{E}_\varepsilon \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\varepsilon_i(Z_i-Z_i') \bigg\|_{\mathcal H}^q. \end{align*} Consequently, \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N\|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} &\le \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \mathbb{E}\,\mathbb{E}_\varepsilon \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\varepsilon_i(Z_i-Z_i') \bigg\|_{\mathcal H}^q \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}= \|S-S'\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)} \le 2\|S\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)}. \end{align*} Here the equality follows because the random vectors \(Z_i-Z_i'\) are independent and symmetric.
nodes.statement_short: Rademacher orthogonality bounds the square function by 2||S||_{L_q}.

nodes.name: Weak moment lower bound
nodes.statement: Moreover, for every \(h\in\mathcal H\) with \(\|h\|_{\mathcal H}=1\), \[ \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle h,Z_i\rangle_{\mathcal H} \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}} = \|\langle h,S\rangle_{\mathcal H}\|_{L_{q/2}} \le \|\langle h,S\rangle_{\mathcal H}\|_{L_q} \le \|S\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)}. \] Therefore, \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^N\|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^2 \bigg)^{1/2} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} + \sup_{\|h\|_{\mathcal H}=1} \bigg\| \sum_{i=1}^N\langle h,Z_i\rangle_{\mathcal H} \bigg\|_{L_{q/2}} \le 3\|S\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)}. \] Together with the upper bound, this completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Weak moments are at most ||S||_{L_q}; combine.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement_short: Upper bounds from Theorem 2.2 (via van Handel's convex domination) and Proposition 2.3; Gaussian lower bounds by testing against v^{otimes p}, (v otimes v) otimes B_perp^{otimes(k-1)} and (Sigma/||Sigma||_F)^{otimes k}.

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian upper bound
nodes.statement: \textbf{Sub-Gaussian upper bound.} \medskip Set \(E:=\operatorname{Ran}(\Sigma)\). Since \(\mathbb{E}\langle v,X\rangle^2=0\) for \(v\in\ker(\Sigma)\), we have \(X\in E\) almost surely. Let \(\Sigma_E\) denote the restriction of \(\Sigma\) to \(E\), and set \(Y:=K^{-1}\Sigma_E^{-1/2}X\). By the definition of the sub-Gaussian constant \(K\), after a universal rescaling \(Y\) satisfies the \(1\)-sub-Gaussian tail convention used in the comparison theorem \cite[Theorem~1.1]{vanhandel2025subgaussian}. Consequently, \(Y\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}CG_E\) with \(G_E\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_E)\) for a universal constant \(C>0\), and since convex order is preserved under linear maps, applying \(C^{-1}\Sigma_E^{1/2}\) to both sides gives \[ (CK)^{-1}X\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}\Sigma_E^{1/2}G_E=G_\Sigma. \] For \(A\in(\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes p}\), define the scalar-valued \(p\)-linear map \(T_A(x_1,\ldots,x_p):=\langle A,x_1\otimes\cdots\otimes x_p\rangle_{\mathsf F}\), whose Frobenius norm is \(\|T_A\|_{\mathsf F}=\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\). Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:main2} to \((CK)^{-1}X\) and \(T_A\), and using the homogeneity of \(T_A\), gives \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} = (CK)^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| T_A\bigl((CK)^{-1}X,\ldots,(CK)^{-1}X\bigr) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\|A\|_{\mathsf F}. \end{align*} Since \(\|V-\mathbb{E} V\|_{L_q}\le2\|V\|_{L_q}\) for every scalar \(V\in L_q\), it follows that \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} &\lesssim_p K^p\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\\ &\asymp_p K^p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt{q}+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases} \end{align*} where the final comparison follows since the terms defining \(\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\) form a geometric progression.
nodes.statement_short: Van Handel's convex domination and Theorem 2.2 applied to T_A.

nodes.name: Convex domination
nodes.statement: Set \(E:=\operatorname{Ran}(\Sigma)\). Since \(\mathbb{E}\langle v,X\rangle^2=0\) for \(v\in\ker(\Sigma)\), we have \(X\in E\) almost surely. Let \(\Sigma_E\) denote the restriction of \(\Sigma\) to \(E\), and set \(Y:=K^{-1}\Sigma_E^{-1/2}X\). By the definition of the sub-Gaussian constant \(K\), after a universal rescaling \(Y\) satisfies the \(1\)-sub-Gaussian tail convention used in the comparison theorem \cite[Theorem~1.1]{vanhandel2025subgaussian}. Consequently, \(Y\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}CG_E\) with \(G_E\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_E)\) for a universal constant \(C>0\), and since convex order is preserved under linear maps, applying \(C^{-1}\Sigma_E^{1/2}\) to both sides gives \[ (CK)^{-1}X\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}\Sigma_E^{1/2}G_E=G_\Sigma. \]
nodes.statement_short: Van Handel's theorem gives (CK)^{-1}X <=_cx G_Sigma.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement: For \(A\in(\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes p}\), define the scalar-valued \(p\)-linear map \(T_A(x_1,\ldots,x_p):=\langle A,x_1\otimes\cdots\otimes x_p\rangle_{\mathsf F}\), whose Frobenius norm is \(\|T_A\|_{\mathsf F}=\|A\|_{\mathsf F}\). Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:main2} to \((CK)^{-1}X\) and \(T_A\), and using the homogeneity of \(T_A\), gives \begin{align*} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} = (CK)^p \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| T_A\bigl((CK)^{-1}X,\ldots,(CK)^{-1}X\bigr) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p K^p\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\|A\|_{\mathsf F}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 2.2 to T_A.

nodes.name: Centering
nodes.statement: Since \(\|V-\mathbb{E} V\|_{L_q}\le2\|V\|_{L_q}\) for every scalar \(V\in L_q\), it follows that \begin{align*} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} &\lesssim_p K^p\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\\ &\asymp_p K^p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt{q}+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases} \end{align*} where the final comparison follows since the terms defining \(\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\) form a geometric progression.
nodes.statement_short: Center and compare Psi_p with its extreme terms.

nodes.name: Gaussian upper bounds
nodes.statement: \textbf{Gaussian upper bounds.} \medskip Now let \(X\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)\). Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:Hilbert-Gaussian-tensor-Lq} with \(\mathcal H=\mathbb R\) and \(T=T_A\), we obtain \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p \Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\|A\|_{\mathsf F}, \] and \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \lesssim_p \Psi_p^\circ(q,\Sigma)\|A\|_{\mathsf F}, \] where \[ \Psi_p(q,\Sigma) = \sum_{\substack{0\le j\le p\\ j\equiv p\;(\mathrm{mod}\,2)}} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-j)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{j/2}q^{j/2}\asymp_p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2} + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}, \end{cases} \] and \[ \Psi_p^\circ(q,\Sigma) = \sum_{\substack{1\le j\le p\\ j\equiv p\;(\mathrm{mod}\,2)}} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-j)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{j/2}q^{j/2}\asymp_p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \] Taking the supremum over \(\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1\) proves the desired upper bounds.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 2.3 with T=T_A.

nodes.name: Gaussian lower bounds
nodes.statement_short: Test against well-chosen tensors.

nodes.name: Diagonalization
nodes.statement: By orthogonal invariance, assume that \[ \Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d), \qquad \lambda_1=\|\Sigma\|, \qquad X=\big(\lambda_1^{1/2}\xi_1,\ldots, \lambda_d^{1/2}\xi_d\big), \] where \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d\) are independent standard Gaussian random variables. We first prove the lower bound for the centered version.
nodes.statement_short: Diagonalize Sigma; start with the centered version.

nodes.name: Highest-chaos lower bound
nodes.statement: Let \(v=e_1\). Testing against \(A=v^{\otimes p}\) gives \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} = \|\Sigma\|^{p/2} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left( \xi_1^p-\mathbb{E}\xi_1^p \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right). \] Since \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \xi_1^p-\mathbb{E}\xi_1^p \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \asymp_p q^{p/2}, \qquad q\ge1, \] we obtain \begin{equation} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \gtrsim_p \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Testing against v^{otimes p} gives ||Sigma||^{p/2}q^{p/2}.

nodes.name: Highest-chaos lower bound (5.1)
nodes.statement: \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \gtrsim_p \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}.
nodes.label: eq:gaussian-directional-highest-chaos-lower

nodes.name: Case sigma_perp large
nodes.statement_short: Intermediate scale when the off-top spectrum carries Frobenius mass.

nodes.name: Open the case
nodes.statement: Set \[ \sigma_{\perp} := \bigg( \sum_{j=2}^d\lambda_j^2 \bigg)^{1/2}. \] Suppose first that $\sigma_{\perp} \ge \frac12\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}$. Define \[ B_{\perp} := \frac{\operatorname{diag}(0,\lambda_2,\ldots,\lambda_d)} {\sigma_{\perp}}, \qquad Q_{\perp}:=X^\top B_{\perp}X. \] Then \[ \|B_{\perp}\|_{\mathsf F}=1, \qquad Q_{\perp} = \frac1{\sigma_{\perp}} \sum_{j=2}^d\lambda_j^2\xi_j^2, \qquad \mathbb{E} Q_{\perp}=\sigma_{\perp}, \] and \(Q_{\perp}\) is independent of \(\xi_1\).
nodes.statement_short: Define sigma_perp, B_perp and Q_perp.

nodes.name: Even p
nodes.statement_short: Test against (v otimes v) otimes B_perp^{otimes(k-1)}.

nodes.name: Even-order intermediate lower bound (5.2)
nodes.label: eq:last_lemma_aux1

nodes.name: Odd p
nodes.statement:
Suppose instead that \(p=2k+1\) is odd. Take $A:=v\otimes B_{\perp}^{\otimes k}$. Then \(\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1\), and \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathsf F}= \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle v,X\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle (X^{	op} B_{\perp} X)^k = \|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\xi_1Q_{\perp}^k. \] This random variable is centered. By independence, Jensen's inequality, and the standard Gaussian moment estimate, we have  egin{align} \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_q} &= \|\Sigma\|^{1/2} \|\xi_1\|_{L_q} \|Q_{\perp}\|_{L_{kq}}^k
onumber\ &\ge \|\Sigma\|^{1/2} \|\xi_1\|_{L_q} (\mathbb{E} Q_{\perp})^k 
onumber\ &= \|\Sigma\|^{1/2} \|\xi_1\|_{L_q} (\sigma_{\perp})^k 
onumber\ &\gtrsim_p \|\Sigma\|^{1/2} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^k \sqrt q. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Test against v otimes B_perp^{otimes k}.

nodes.name: Odd-order intermediate lower bound (5.3)
nodes.statement:
\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\mathopen{}\mathclose group\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupightangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroupight\|_{L_q} &= \|\Sigma\|^{1/2} \|\xi_1\|_{L_q} \|Q_{\perp}\|_{L_{kq}}^k
onumber\ &\ge \|\Sigma\|^{1/2} \|\xi_1\|_{L_q} (\mathbb{E} Q_{\perp})^k 
onumber\ &= \|\Sigma\|^{1/2} \|\xi_1\|_{L_q} (\sigma_{\perp})^k 
onumber\ &\gtrsim_p \|\Sigma\|^{1/2} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^k \sqrt q.
nodes.label: eq:last_lemma_aux2

nodes.name: Conclude the case
nodes.statement: Together with \eqref{eq:gaussian-directional-highest-chaos-lower}, the bounds \eqref{eq:last_lemma_aux1} and \eqref{eq:last_lemma_aux2} prove the lower bound when \(\sigma_{\perp}\ge\frac12\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}\).
nodes.statement_short: Combine with (5.1).

nodes.name: Case sigma_perp small
nodes.statement: It remains to consider $\sigma_{\perp} < \frac12\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}$. Since $\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^2 = \|\Sigma\|^2+\sigma_{\perp}^2$, this gives $\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F} \le \frac{2}{\sqrt3}\|\Sigma\|$, and consequently \[ \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|q \lesssim_p\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, \qquad \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt q \lesssim_p\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}. \] Therefore \eqref{eq:gaussian-directional-highest-chaos-lower} already dominates the intermediate scale in this case, which completes the proof of the centered lower bound.
nodes.statement_short: Then ||Sigma||_F ~ ||Sigma|| and (5.1) dominates.

nodes.name: Non-centered version
nodes.statement: We now turn to the non-centered version. Since \(\|V-\mathbb{E} V\|_{L_q}\le2\|V\|_{L_q}\) for every scalar \(V\in L_q\), the centered lower bound just established gives \begin{equation} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \gtrsim_p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{equation} When \(p\) is odd, this is the desired bound. Suppose then that \(p=2k\) is even, and set \[ B:=\frac{\Sigma}{\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}}, \qquad A:=B^{\otimes k}, \] so that \(\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=\|B\|_{\mathsf F}^k=1\) and \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle B^{\otimes k},X^{\otimes 2k}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(X^\top B X\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^k = \bigg( \frac1{\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}} \sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j^2\xi_j^2 \bigg)^{k} \ge0. \] Since \(X^\top B X\ge0\) with \(\mathbb{E} X^\top B X=\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}\), monotonicity of \(L_q\)-norms and Jensen's inequality give \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \ge \mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(X^\top B X\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^k \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E} X^\top B X\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^k = \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}. \end{equation} Combining \eqref{eq:last_lemma_aux3} and \eqref{eq:last_lemma_aux4}, and noting that \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|q \lesssim_p\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}\), we obtain, for \(p\) even, \[ \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \gtrsim_p \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}. \] This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Deduce from the centered bound plus a trace test at even orders.

nodes.name: Reduce to the centered bound
nodes.statement: We now turn to the non-centered version. Since \(\|V-\mathbb{E} V\|_{L_q}\le2\|V\|_{L_q}\) for every scalar \(V\in L_q\), the centered lower bound just established gives \begin{equation} \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \gtrsim_p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{equation} When \(p\) is odd, this is the desired bound.
nodes.statement_short: Centering costs a factor 2.

nodes.name: Non-centered lower bound from the centered one (5.4)
nodes.statement: \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \gtrsim_p \begin{cases} \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt] \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt q + \|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}, & p \text{ odd}. \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:last_lemma_aux3

nodes.name: Even-order trace scale
nodes.statement: Suppose then that \(p=2k\) is even, and set \[ B:=\frac{\Sigma}{\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}}, \qquad A:=B^{\otimes k}, \] so that \(\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=\|B\|_{\mathsf F}^k=1\) and \[ \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle B^{\otimes k},X^{\otimes 2k}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} = \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(X^\top B X\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^k = \bigg( \frac1{\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}} \sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j^2\xi_j^2 \bigg)^{k} \ge0. \] Since \(X^\top B X\ge0\) with \(\mathbb{E} X^\top B X=\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}\), monotonicity of \(L_q\)-norms and Jensen's inequality give \begin{equation} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \ge \mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(X^\top B X\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^k \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E} X^\top B X\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^k = \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}. \end{equation} Combining \eqref{eq:last_lemma_aux3} and \eqref{eq:last_lemma_aux4}, and noting that \(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|q \lesssim_p\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}\), we obtain, for \(p\) even, \[ \sup_{\|A\|_{\mathsf F}=1} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \gtrsim_p \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}+\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}q^{p/2}. \] This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Testing against (Sigma/||Sigma||_F)^{otimes k} gives ||Sigma||_F^{p/2}.

nodes.name: Even-order non-centered trace lower bound (5.5)
nodes.statement: \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\| \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,X^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q} \ge \mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(X^\top B X\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^k \ge \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E} X^\top B X\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^k = \|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}.
nodes.label: eq:last_lemma_aux4
